FR-001.title: A partial work order offers its matches in a modal

FR-002.title: The modal appears only when the entry is not a complete resolvable work order

FR-003.title: A complete work order is formatted and used directly with no modal

FR-004.title: The accepted input forms and the formatting rule are unchanged

FR-005.title: A partial becomes the prefix plus a trailing wildcard

FR-006.title: A partial is never padded to six digits

FR-007.title: Matches are shown recognisably with enough context to choose

FR-008.title: Choosing a match sets the entry and continues the flow

FR-009.title: Dismissing leaves the entry and flow unchanged and does not trap

FR-010.title: No matches is reported plainly with a way to retry

FR-011.title: An unshowable result stays usable and states how many matched

FR-012.title: One shared capability holds the matching; the entry step holds none

FR-013.title: The capability takes a caller-described source and knows nothing of work orders

FR-014.title: A new searchable source is additive and needs no change to the capability

FR-015.title: An unknown source is reported unavailable never silently empty

FR-016.title: Trigger pattern and match count are the caller to state

FR-017.title: Matching is case-insensitive and tolerates the separators typed

FR-018.title: Stored-procedure-first with no run-time-assembled statement text

FR-019.title: External search keeps the cached fallback and an empty result is a real answer

FR-020.title: Every schema artifact ships its rollback and the master lists stay in sync

FR-021.title: Every user-visible string comes through the resource mechanism

FR-022.title: The existing rejection for an impossible entry is preserved

intent: Let a person find a work order by typing only part of it, through one shared picker that any screen can point at its own list.
context: area: Module_Setup/Views/SetupWorkOrderPage.xaml + MTM_Waitlist.Setup/ViewModels/SetupWorkOrderViewModel.cs - the entry step and its existing LostFocus on-blur search
area: MTM_Waitlist.Setup/Services/WorkOrderValidationService.cs - the normalisation rule this builds on (^(?:WO-)?(\d{5,6})$, padded to six)
area: MTM_Waitlist.Setup/Services/SetupWorkflowService.cs - existing Levenshtein best-match helper, candidate for reuse
area: MTM_Waitlist.Mock read-shape fallback + Database/Mock - the boundary for searching a list outside our own stores
constraint: constitution III stored-procedure-first; no inline or run-time-assembled statement text
expectations: out of scope: the picker ships one caller - a second caller is follow-on work
not changing: the existing work order formatting rule and accepted input forms
not in scope: a second source of truth for what a work order is
out of scope: contains-anywhere matching as the default - prefix is the chosen reading
owner action, not the agent: reinstalling the database from seed
